learning: Span 6 to 8 cm gave no change in line losses or max_error. Read the 10 cm result against that: if losses still persist, move to the drivetrain rather than widening further.
notes: Isolates the span test: the Builder's 10 cm span (±0.05 outer, ±0.025 inner) with the iteration 1 controller unchanged. Nothing else varies, so any change in line losses or max_error comes from the span.
rationale: Iterations 0 and 1 both ended with every trial off track after one line-loss event, with max_error near 0.061 to 0.063 m, progress 0.11 to 0.17 and no finishes. Widening the span from 6 cm to 8 cm changed nothing, so span is not yet the limit at those widths. The Builder's test here is a 10 cm span (outer sensors at ±0.05 m, inner at ±0.025 m), with the footprint, forward offset, body and drivetrain unchanged. I keep the controller from iteration 1 (kp 1.0, kd 0.2, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.0, last_direction) so this race isolates the sensor span. Sensor weights stay at [-2,-1,0,1,2], which keeps the signal scale the same. Expected result if span is the limit: line_loss_events falls toward 0 and max_error drops below 0.06 m on the tight bends. If losses and max_error stay near 0.06 m, the next change should be the drivetrain (wheel_track 0.10 m), as the Integrator's pre-specified branch says.
